newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Court sides with church on Jesus film, Bibles.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Court sides with church on Jesus film, Bibles.

text.p: The Supreme Court Monday upheld an appeal against the city of Albuquerque and allowed a New Mexico church to use a city-owned building to show a film about the life of Jesus and to distribute Bibles.

The justices let stand a federal appeals court ruling that Albuquerque had failed to show a compelling interest justifying its policy barring sectarian instruction and religious worship at the city's senior centres. The appeals court in May struck down the policy as an unconstitutional restriction on expression.

The case began in 1994 when Don Kimbro, pastor at the evangelical Church on the Rock, wanted to show a two-hour film entitled Jesus and to distribute large-print Bibles at one of six city-owned and operated senior centres.
The city denied the request, citing a federal law that provides funding for senior centres but requires that they not be used for sectarian instruction or religious worship.

The church sued, saying the city allowed the senior centres to be used for a wide variety of public events. A federal judge ruled for the city but the appeals court said Albuquerque's policy constituted viewpoint discrimination.

The city appealed to the high court, saying "Congress may prohibit core religious activities in federally funded senior centres consistent with this court's current view" of the First Amendment freedom of speech and religion guarantees.
But the high court sided with the church, rejecting the city's appeal without any comment or dissent.
